chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited usury (riba) so that people would not refrain from doing good deeds.

key_terms.اصْطِنَاعِ الْمَعْرُوفِ: Doing good deeds or performing charity/kindness
key_terms.الرِّبَا: Usury or interest, a financial transaction involving guaranteed increase on a loan
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic, an honorific title for God

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah prohibit riba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that the prohibition of riba is rooted in preserving social solidarity, ensuring that wealth circulation does not become so burdensome that it prevents individuals from performing *ihsan* (good deeds) and charity. This perspective highlights the socio-economic wisdom of the prohibition, linking financial justice directly to the preservation of communal bonds and the flow of benevolence in society.
